against starvation. Skeletal muscles also become more efficient, so that they need less energy to 
fuel their movement. Additionally, after weight loss, there is less physical mass of the body that has 
to be moved from place to place throughout the day, resulting in fewer calories burned through 
physical movement and activity, and less metabolically active tissue using calories for fuel throughout 
the day. These metabolic changes conserve energy, reducing the “energy out” side of the energy

balance equation and favoring weight regain.16,17 In individuals maintaining a 10% or greater weight 
loss, these changes combine to account for an estimated decrease of 300-400 calories in energy 
expenditure per day beyond what is expected due to the change in body composition alone.18 
On the “energy in” side of the equation, neurological and hormonal changes also increase appetite, 
lower satiety, and increase the brain’s focus on obtaining food. Researchers have estimated that 
weight loss of about 2 pounds increases appetite by about 95 calories per day.16,17 These biological 
factors and their influence on weight are discussed further in the video below.
